title: Graceful burst quota stitcher and latency budget allocator
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: Several customers reported uneven burst exhaustion when contention spikes hit mixed-priority tenants. Today the warm-pool and burst token systems operate independently of latency SLO signals which produces abrupt shedding. This PR introduces a controller (burst-quota-stitcher) plus a complementary latency-budget-allocator that ties ephemeral burst credit redistribution to observed p50/p95 latency pressure. Goals: 1) smooth user-visible degradation when pool pressure rises, 2) prioritize low-latency traffic by temporarily reweighting ephemeral credits, 3) surface telemetry for post-mortem and capacity planning. Implementation summary: - New controller: controllers/burst_stitcher.go; periodically samples per-tenant utilization + latency histograms and proposes cross-tenant stitch operations (soft transfer of ephemeral credits) with safety checks and cooldown windows. - Latency budget allocator: scheduler/latency_budget_allocator.go implements a moving-window algebra that converts target latency headroom into a soft throughput ceiling and recommended burst holdback. - Decisioning: stitch operations are conservative by default (max 5% cross-tenant transfer per epoch) and include a trial canary path where transfers are flagged but not applied (opt-in via feature flag). - Telemetry: added metrics (redwood.burst.stitch{phase,decision,recover}) and event logs (burst.stitch.events) to help debug transfers; introduced an annotation on tenant objects recording last-stitch-reason. - Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind enableBurstStitch; initial rollout to internal staging, then opt-in customers, then broad rollout with automatic backoff if latency increases. Backwards compatibility: no schema breaking changes to tenant objects; new annotations are optional. This PR description includes checklist and test plan. Checklist: - [x] Controller logic and unit tests - [x] Integration test in perf-canary harness that simulates mixed-priority spike - [x] Telemetry and dashboards wiring - [x] Feature flag gating and safe defaults - [x] Documentation snippet for ops console (rollout notes) Test plan: Run perf-canary scenario that creates two tenants (prod-high, prod-low) and emits a steady background workload to reserve capacity, then a sudden spike on low-priority tenant. Expectation: stitcher will move ephemeral credits away from low-priority tenant gradually, p95 on high-priority tenant remains within target, and stitch events appear in telemetry. Linear/Jira links included in metadata. Note: this PR intentionally limits transfer volume per epoch to avoid oscillation; follow-ups will introduce adaptive decay curves and an admission controller for cross-cluster transfers.
